question: In January 2025, the Reserve Bank of India removed supervisory restrictions on which of the following Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arohan Financial Services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, in **January 2025**, lifted the supervisory restrictions on **Arohan Financial Services**, allowing the firm to resume its **sanction and disbursement** of loans.
 
• These restrictions were originally imposed on **October 17, 2024**, due to concerns regarding **usurious interest rates** and non-compliance with the regulatory framework for **microfinance loans**.
 
• The **central bank** had observed that the **Weighted Average Lending Rate (WALR)** and the interest margins charged by the company were significantly higher than the benchmarks, violating **Fair Practices Code** guidelines.
 
• Alongside **Arohan Financial Services**, the **RBI** also removed similar curbs on **Asirvad Microfinance** and **DMI Finance** in early **January 2025** after they demonstrated improvement in their pricing policies.
 
• The lifting of the **"cease and desist"** order signifies that the company has aligned its **internal control systems** and **pricing mechanisms** with the **RBI’s** regulatory expectations for **NBFC-MFIs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Regulatory Framework for NBFCs:**
 
 
• The **RBI** exercises its powers under **Section 45L(1)(b)** of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, to issue directions to **Non-Banking Financial Companies** to ensure financial stability.
 
• In **2024**, the **RBI** intensified its scrutiny on the **microfinance sector** to prevent **excessive interest rates** and ensure that the benefits of low-cost funding are passed to **low-income borrowers**.
 
 
 
• **Arohan Financial Services:**
 
 
• Headquartered in **Kolkata**, **West Bengal**, it is a prominent **NBFC-MFI** (Micro Finance Institution) serving the **under-banked** populations in **India**.
 
• The organization primarily focuses on providing **credit facilities** to women in **rural and semi-urban** areas for income-generating activities.
 
 
 
• **The October 2024 Action:**
 
 
• In a rare move, the **RBI** had simultaneously barred **four NBFCs**—**Navi Finserv**, **Asirvad Microfinance**, **Arohan Financial Services**, and **DMI Finance**—from loan disbursements.
 
• The action was part of a broader **supervisory campaign** to curb **irresponsible lending** and ensure that **digital lenders** and **MFIs** maintain **transparency** in their **Annual Percentage Rate (APR)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Microfinance Pricing Policy:** Under the **RBI’s** **March 2022** regulatory framework, **NBFC-MFIs** have the freedom to set interest rates but must ensure they are not **usurious**. The **Board-approved** policy must include a transparent **pricing model**.
 
• **Impact of Curbs:** The imposition of curbs usually leads to a temporary halt in **Asset Under Management (AUM)** growth and affects the **liquidity** and **credit ratings** of the concerned entities.
 
• **Compliance:** To have restrictions removed, entities must provide **written commitments** and audit reports confirming that their **lending practices** and **customer protection** measures are in full compliance with **RBI** norms.

cb:T24
